A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same PatchGuard study. Their main text, equations, Figures 1-4, Tables 1-21, and Appendices A-L support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original clean and adversarial anomaly detection/localization experiments on eight datasets, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and per-class appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the main benchmark evaluations and supplementary analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: Foreground-aware pseudo-anomaly generation, the ViT and attention discriminator, regularization, adversarial training, and inference remain unchanged. Section 5.1 adds a supporting citation without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same tasks and scenarios on MVTec AD, VisA, BTAD, MPDD, WFDD, DTD-Synthetic, Head-CT, and BraTS2021. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1-3 and the pseudo-anomaly generator comparison in Table 6. The newly cited teacher-student work is not introduced as an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Both retain AUROC evaluation, PGD-10 training and PGD-1000 testing at epsilon 8/255, and the same additional attack evaluations. Model configurations, preprocessing, budgets, and appendix protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 7 and Appendices C, I, and J retain the same regularization, generator, backbone, sparse-attention, discriminator, and attack-strength analyses. No ablation, robustness test, or qualitative case study changes.

E5.justification: Tables 1-21 retain the same point-estimate AUROC reporting. No repeated-run counts, seed information, uncertainty estimates, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Numerical and qualitative results match throughout. PatchGuard's average clean/adversarial AUROCs remain 89.3/74.1 for detection in Table 1 and 94.8/81.1 for localization in Table 2; appendix results and figure images also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Section 4 attention and pseudoinverse derivation, and Equations 1-7 remain unchanged. Differences in extracted mathematical spacing do not represent revised reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty, robustness, pseudo-anomaly generation, and attention-regularization claims, including the same claimed performance improvements.

C2.justification: The robustness interpretations and clean-performance tradeoff remain unchanged. Appendix K retains the pretrained-model dependence and lack of foreground-identification guarantees; Appendix L retains the same detection/localization attack discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix G retains AdamW, learning rate 0.0008, 300 epochs, batch size 16, 224-by-224 inputs, and top-k of 5. Augmentation details, attack adaptations, and the code-link destination also remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Mirzaei et al. (2025), 'A contrastive teacher-student framework for novelty detection under style shifts,' as reference 61 in Section 5.1's hard-transformation citation list. Other research positioning is unchanged.

P1.justification: Editorial changes are limited to citation renumbering and the arXiv version/date marker. The prose, terminology, section organization, and appendix order are retained.

P2.justification: The added reference causes limited reflow in Section 5.1 and the bibliography, including a short second-column continuation on PDF page 12. Figures 1-4 and Tables 1-21 retain their designs and placements.

improvement.justification: The added citation modestly broadens attribution for the existing hard-augmentation rationale. Scientific explanations, methods, evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain unchanged, while the small layout shifts do not materially affect readability. There is no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
